prompt: Two triangular ramps have two pairs of proportional sides, and the angles BETWEEN those pairs of sides are congruent. Which similarity criterion applies? Answer with three letters.
hint: Read the parts in order around the triangle: side, angle, side.

hints.text: Read the parts in order around the triangle: side, angle, side.
The angle is included between the two proportional sides.

explanation: The three similarity criteria are AA, SSS (all three pairs of sides proportional), and SAS (two pairs proportional with the included angle congruent).
Here two pairs of sides are proportional and the included angles are congruent, so it is SAS similarity.
Note the difference from SAS congruence: sides here are PROPORTIONAL, not equal — only the angle must actually be congruent.

alternativeExplanations.title: Congruence vs similarity, same letters
steps: SSS and SAS appear on both lists, but with a swap: congruence demands equal sides, similarity only demands a constant ratio.
Angles never scale, so in both versions the angle must be congruent.
